publications.title: Protecting The Brand: Counterfeiting and Grey Markets
publications.description:
A company's brands are often its most valuable assets.  They're also a rich target for counterfeiters.  With the global value of counterfeit goods estimated at as much as $500-600 billion annually, companies must make a significant effort to combat counterfeiters, gray marketers and cyber squatters.

This uniquely valuable treatise is designed to help in-house and outside counsel as well as corporate and marketing executives understand the full scope of the problem and take preventive measures.  It also explains, in detail, the strategies available when violations have already occurred.  Topics covered include:
Problems caused by counterfeit and gray market goods
Specific industry case studies
Proactive internal procedures to combat counterfeiting and the gray market
Using the Lanham Act to combat gray and counterfeit goods
Trademark infringement and dilution
Copyright piracy enforcement and recent developments
Issues relating to websites
International remedies

Protecting the value of a brand and protecting consumers from substandard, even dangerous, imitations requires every legal weapon available, in the U.S. and internationally. Protecting the Brand: Counterfeiting and Gray Markets is an essential part of that arsenal

projects.title: MILSOFT WindMil analysis of distribution feeder and study of impact of PV penetration
projects.description:
The project consisted of Three phases which were:
Part 1 - Modelling a Distribution System in Milsoft WindMil
Part 2 - Cost efficient feeder conditioning analysis to reduce line losses and to control voltage drop by load balancing and subsequent addition of Voltage Regulators, Capacitors and Re-conductoring using Milsoft WindMil.
Part 3 - Studying the impact of Distributed Photovoltaic Generation on Residential Distribution Systems. It included analysis of improvement in voltage unbalance, line losses and voltage profile when system is exposed to high and low PV penetration levels at various system loading.

projects.title: Lightning Strike Analysis and Insulation Coordination Study of 275 KV Substation
projects.description: Assembled Bergeron line model for modelling towers and developed a 275 KV substation layout. Simulated lightning surge of 1.2/50 50kA and analyzed its effect on substation elements. Also simulated backflashover and analyzed overvoltages caused due to it. Deduced desired BIL rating for various substation elements based on results obtained.

projects.title: SCADA Master & Substation Data-Concentrator Communication Scheme
projects.description: Configured SEL- RTAC as a data concentrator and made it communicate with SEL-451 over TCP/IP and SEL-651 over serial Radio simultaneously. The SCADA master was simulated by NI Lab VIEW which polled the RTAC.DNP3 point lists comprising of both analog and binary points were configured for the relays and the RTAC. Remote and manual breaker operations were performed and the data sent to the SCADA master was analyzed using Wireshark. Unsolicited responses were generated by breaker operation and also by varying adjustable transformer tap positions.

projects.title: IEC 61850 GOOSE Messaging
projects.description: Configured GOOSE messaging between SEL-451 and SEL-651R. A GOOSE message was triggered by using the Pushbutton on SEL-451 to which the SEL-651R subscribed and in turn published a GOOSE message to SEL-451

headline: Global Client Service Partner | MedTech & Healthcare
about:
As a Client Service Partner at EY, I lead teams dedicated to serving our largest global clients, particularly in the life sciences and healthcare sectors. My role is centered on understanding and adapting to each client's unique culture and operating style and driving our teams to tailor solutions that deliver measurable outcomes, strengthen stakeholder relationships, and enhance brand value. With a steadfast commitment to innovation and collaboration, I draw upon my extensive experience in business and consulting—spanning strategy, transformation, technology, transactions, commercial excellence and operational effectiveness—to tackle complex challenges and empower our clients in their pursuit of groundbreaking advancements in quality healthcare.

I have developed extensive expertise in architecting and executing complex business transformations across the supply and demand continuum, including the detailed development of strategic business cases, program governance structures, and change management cadences. My work encompasses multiple transactions in the MedTech, consumer products, and technology sectors, including cross functional preparation for a strategic sale, a private equity sale, and an IPO. Additionally, I led programs for a global manufacturer to consolidate distributors, refined governance for a $10B+ member owned cooperative, executed a supply chain transformation for a MedTech company, and implemented an enterprise cost transformation that resulted in a post-sale synergy plan.

With over three decades of experience, I have cultivated a reputation as a strategic and empathetic leader. My passion lies in creating inclusive environments that enable both teams and individuals to flourish. A cornerstone of my role is nurturing the next generation of leaders; I take great pride in mentoring both client and EY executives, guiding them on their career journeys and fostering their professional growth.

experience.description:
As a senior client service partner, I advance relationships with C-suite leaders by addressing their growth and operational challenges. I leverage my depth in governance, operating models, and organizational culture to enhance outcomes for their customers and stakeholders. My success stems from recruiting and empowering a diverse team of EY professionals and alliance partners to cultivate an exceptional client experience.

I continue to serve as a trusted advisor to senior management on acquisitions, divestitures, operating models, innovation, and cost improvement programs. Leveraging my cross-industry experience and extensive EY network, I excel at distilling complex issues into critical questions and aligning incentives to achieve desired outcomes.

As the inaugural leader of the EY Global MedTech sector, I developed the strategy for this new group serving MedTech clients across all EY disciplines. I fostered strong connections with EY teams in healthcare, industrial manufacturing, consumer products, and digital health, while advising our client teams serving established and emerging MedTech companies.

I was also the primary sponsor and contributing author for EY's Pulse of the MedTech Industry Annual Report. For the past 19 years, the Pulse Report has been a highly anticipated and widely read analysis of MedTech industry issues, disruptive forces, and future trends, released annually at Advamed's MedTech Conference via a keynote CEO panel that I have moderated many times.

headline: EY Global Client Service Partner
about:
As a Senior Partner at EY, I serve as the Global Account Partner for one of the largest Consumer Products and Pet Care companies in the world. I focus on understanding the personal and professional motivations of the clients we serve and then aligning EY teams to meet their specific needs in both content and culture.

I am dedicated to helping clients learn from others, connect internal resources, mitigate risks, and achieve their desired outcomes. The greatest satisfaction comes from earning the opportunity to serve my clients repeatedly and receiving referrals based on trust, authenticity, and a deep understanding of their culture.

In addition to building diverse teams across geographies to tackle transformative objectives, my consulting expertise lies in connecting business strategy with operating models and talent frameworks, maximizing the potential of the total workforce. I work in both Transformations and Transactions (M&A).

Previously, I led the EY People Advisory Services business for the US-East Region, where I doubled revenue and grew the team to close to 500 practitioners in just four years. I also worked across the US Regions and LATAM to help scale our People Advisory practices in those regions, following my playbook.  Before EY, I was Vice President and leader of Booz Allen’s Strategic Human Capital and Talent Management consulting business. I have authored several thought pieces and taught at Georgetown University and Emory University within their MBA programs.

I hold an MBA from Emory University, a B.S. in Finance from Bradley University, and multiple Master's Certificates, including Mergers & Acquisitions from the University of Chicago, Big Data Analytics from Harvard Business School, and the EY Strategic Leadership Program from Harvard Business School

experience.description:

- Technology-enabled transformation

I serve functions across the organization, including GBS, Finance, Controller, Tax, HR, IT, Data & Analytics, Supply Chain, R&D, Procurement, Distribution & Logistics, and Strategy.

I was responsible for growing the total EY business across all Service Lines for B2B companies, including consulting firms, law firms, and business services companies. My market encompassed over 600 clients, offering a mix of audit and non-audit services. I had the privilege of working with an outstanding team of Partners, Managing Directors, Directors and Senior Managers —professionally the best in the business and even better human beings. Together, we supported each other's success and strived to help our clients differentiate themselves in their pursuit of market growth.

I personally believe that our global EY network have a lot to offer to clients and that we can team up to provide measurable and sustainable value. In my role as Manager in Business Consulting with EY Ireland, I am responsible for the development of target operating models, Global Business Services (GBS)/ Shared Services design set-up, benchmark generation/analysis and overall transformation activity for the Consulting team. 

I'm a detail oriented, highly efficient professional with a strong and varied background in Stakeholder management and Process improvement. A passionate strategic thinker and team lead, driven to empower private and public organisations to achieve commercial business objectives through leading business initiatives.

Prior to joining EY, I founded and managed Fódla - a Sustainable Clothing start-up. topSkills: Organizational Development
about:
A seasoned consulting leader with 17+ years of global consulting experience, and a strong track record in business development and solution delivery across multiple areas and industries. I have advised leading government officials, C-Suite executives, and helped CXOs and leaders strengthen their business strategy and improve execution, and create a people agenda in strong alignment with business strategy. I have built deep expertise in a broad range of areas such as strategy, culture transformation, organization development, talent management, performance management, leadership development, executive coaching, diversity and inclusion, change management, facilitation, moderation, and intervention, in addition to workforce planning, succession planning, diversity and inclusion, and learning strategy design. Among the positions I have occupied are Partner at Korn Ferry, Director of People and Change at PwC Middle East working closely with the public sector practice, and Senior Manager at Deloitte Consulting LLP. Throughout my career, I have delivered value to C-suite executives in the USA and internationally (USA, UK, UAE, KSA, Qatar, Jordan, Kuwait, and Lebanon). Among my significant achievements was acting as a core team advocate for the Avian Influenza pandemic preparedness and response planning initiative at the White House in Washington D.C. during President Bush’s Administration.

I dedicated two years of my graduate work at Harvard University to studying transformational leadership and resilience, and I also have a keen interest in psychology and neuroscience and the practical applications of these fields on improving decision making, organizational learning and performance.

experience.description: The Institute of Coaching is a non-profit organization dedicated to enhancing the integrity and credibility of the field of coaching by awarding $100,000 in research grants each year thanks to the thought leadership and generous donation from Institute founder and benefactor Ruth Ann Harnisch of The Harnisch Foundation. By advancing coaching research, education, and practice, the Institute supports professional coaches and others who use coaching skills in their personal and professional lives. We are building a global coaching research community by bringing together leaders in the field to accelerate research progress and disseminate coaching's best practices. Coaching is a change process that mobilizes strengths and realizes the potential of individuals and organizations. The practice of coaching embodies a unique skill set designed to optimize the performance of a person or organization in diverse arenas including leadership, healthcare, and public service.

She has delivered value to C-suite executives both with international clients (UK, France, Italy, Romania, Cyprus, Jordan, Kuwait, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Dubai, North Africa, and Lebanon) and US-based clients (Minneapolis, Indianapolis, Washington DC, Chicago, New York, and Iowa).

publications.title: Team Management Systems and Talent Management: A shift in mindset
publications.publishedAt: By Niam Sinno. Copyright © Niam Sinno. All rights reserved.
publications.description:
"Talent management strategies must be built around the things that generate the most value and matter most to employees." Deloitte POV1

Of the two following views, which is nearest to your own situation?


1."My job is interesting, demanding and challenging. It suits the way I like to work." 
2."My job is a means to an end. I do it because I need to earn some money, not because I enjoy it." 
If you agree with the first view, then it is likely that the demands of your job and your work preferences are closely aligned, unlike those in the second person's view. Work preferences are key factors governing the work interests of you and others. They impact on the way we do our jobs, and why we search out certain types of work and avoid others. They influence the extent to which people will stay in a job and give of their best. They are powerful emotional factors that managers and organizations need to be aware of and manage.

publications.title: Contemporary Implications of the 1971 Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act
publications.publishedAt: Perspectives on Business and Economics - New Frontiers for Alaska · May 22, 2022
publications.description: The Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act of 1971 (ANCSA) was created in order to provide economic prosperity for Alaska Natives. However, the modern needs of Alaska Natives have drastically changed and so must the act. This article proposes amendments to ANCSA, namely, the expansion of subsistence living rights; a deeper examination of Alaska Native land ownership; and the adoption of sustainable development approaches that take into account the community’s economic, social, and environmental needs.

honorsAndAwards.description: The President’s Scholar Program recognizes outstanding academic achievement by undergraduate students by providing a fifth year (i.e., a 9th and 10th terms) of study free of tuition. An overall GPA in Lehigh University graded coursework of at least a 3.75 at the time of application for the Scholarship. If the application is approved, the student must also have an overall GPA of 3.75 at the beginning of the Scholarship year.

honorsAndAwards.description: The Eckardt Scholars Program is a highly selective and unique honors program in the College of Arts and Sciences. The program emphasizes deep intellectual curiosity, independent work, and close mentoring relationships between the very highest achieving students and faculty at Lehigh. Students in the program are exempt from the Arts & Sciences distribution requirements and work with their major advisor and the Eckardt Scholars Program Director to create a flexible course of study that best suits their academic interests and ambitions. Although exempt from Arts and Sciences distribution requirements, students will complete the requisite number of credits for their degrees and all correlative requirements for their departmental or interdisciplinary majors. The program includes participation in two Eckardt Scholar Seminars, and completion of a large independent project (in the form of a thesis, artistic creation, or other capstone experience) during the senior year.

about:
Brian Huston is a Principal in the Digital Risk practice of EY within the Chicago, IL office. He also serves as the Americas Digital Compliance Solution leader and EY’s HITRUST service offering leader. Brian specializes in cyber security, privacy, and regulatory compliance, specifically within the healthcare and technology sectors. Brian focuses on identifying, managing, and delivering high-quality consulting services, while also bringing relevant insights and industry experiences. 

Brian leads initiatives which helps organizations understand, mature, and establish cyber security and privacy capabilities that are effective and capable of withstanding external scrutiny (e.g., HITRUST certifications, ISO standard audits, CMMC (Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification) C3PAO audits, system and organization controls (SOC) reports, etc.). His efforts also support organizations to demonstrate compliance with regulations focused on the security and privacy of data (e.g., Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA), General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), etc.). Brian often advises teams on matters related to data privacy and regulatory compliance during merger and acquisition deals. Brian delivers pre-acquisition due diligence engagements for organizations including top private equity firms and Fortune 100 companies, focusing on data privacy and regulatory risks.

During the fall of 2015, Brian joined the Management Information System (MIS) Board of Advisors in the Eller College of Management at the University of Arizona. As part of the Board of Advisors, Brian is able to be a part of a team that helps move the MIS program with its three basic missions: educate students, conduct research, and engage in outreach activities.

headline: EY retired principal

location.linkedinText: Washington, District of Columbia, United States

about:
Before retiring, I led EY's National Tax Department. Prior to re-joining EY in 2011, I served at the US Treasury Department as the Assistant Secretary for Tax Policy, heading the Office of Tax Policy and advising Treasury Secretary Timothy Geithner on all matters relating to taxation. Prior to my appointment as Assistant Secretary in 2009, I was the Deputy Assistant Treasury Secretary for International Tax Affairs. 

I began my career practicing tax law in 1993, at the New York law firm Sullivan & Cromwell, before moving to the Treasury Department, in 1997. I left the Treasury Department, in 2002, as the Deputy International Tax Counsel, and began working at EY, where I was a Partner in the International Tax Services group of EY’s National Tax Department, in Washington, DC, until 2007, when I returned to the Treasury Department.

I received my bachelor’s degree from Columbia University in 1986, my master's degree from the University of Chicago in 1988, my J.D. from the University of California Berkeley in 1992, and my LL.M. from the University of Miami in 1997. 

I have more than 20 years' experience in tax policy and tax planning, both in the private sector and the government. My specialties include global and US tax policy and international tax planning. I am based in Washington, DC.

I am a Manager in EY's Climate Change and Sustainability Services (CCaSS) practice with experience supporting a diverse range of clients on ESG strategy, measurement and reporting. With a background in finance, my approach to sustainability combines comprehensive, long-term business considerations and stakeholder engagement to develop ESG programs that drive returns and enhanced risk management alongside environmental and social impact.  

I have experience with all aspects of ESG program management, including developing sustainability strategies and performance improvement roadmaps, engaging and analyzing ESG rating agencies, performing materiality assessments, performing ESG risk assessments, identifying, measuring, and reporting environmental and social KPIs and targets (including GHG emission identification/scoping and calculation), development of ESG/sustainability reports, website disclosures and policies, and more. In addition, I have experience with emerging ESG frameworks, including the Task Force for Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB), the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), the World Economic Forum's Measuring Stakeholder Capitalism framework, and the World Resources Institute's Greenhouse Gas Protocol

experience.description:
I am a Senior in the Climate Change and Sustainability Services practice at EY - in this role, I support clients with sustainability strategy and reporting, including:
- ESG strategy and planning, including performing materiality assessments, incorporating ESG objectives into enterprise strategy, and developing short (1-2 years) and long (5-10 years) roadmaps for ESG program development, with consideration for program ROI
- ESG risk assessment, including assessing overall and function-specific risk related to environmental and social topics. Experience includes but is not limited to climate risk assessment in alignment to the Task Force for Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) and the Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP)
- ESG measurement, including identification, calculation method development, calculation and monitoring software and tools, and more. In particular, experience with Greenhouse Gas emissions measurement and calculation, including in-depth familiarity with the WRI's GHG Protocol
- ESG stakeholder engagement and analysis, including engagement with large institutional investors and investor proxies, particularly ESG rating agencies such as MSCI and Sustainalytics

about:
Jennifer is a trusted advisor focused on navigating complicated transaction and operational decisions.  To deliver meaningful advice, she draws upon a unique combination of modeling & analytics, investment banking, asset management and accounting experience to help clients accelerate growth and profitability.  Change is the environment of business today, and Jennifer embraces adaptive decision-making to build for the future. 

Currently, Jennifer applies her technical expertise in corporate finance and modeling to advise clients on the financial impact of major decisions, helping them to make more informed decisions.  Her specialty is a data-driven approach that generates value through forecasting, strategic options analysis, capital allocation, scenario planning, acquisition analysis, and post transaction consolidation models.

Previously, she had successfully executed an array of innovative transactions involving mergers & acquisitions (M&A), initial public offerings (IPOs), debt and equity follow-on offerings, and private placements.

Jennifer.Gerold@ey.com
